description: A real author-styled card (flex column, padding, border, background) with a heading and a paragraph child, validating the whole tree compiles/lays out/paints correctly against Chromium, not just a bare default element.

florui.css: .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 240px; padding-top: 16px; padding-right: 16px; padding-bottom: 16px; padding-left: 16px; border-top-width: 1px; border-top-style: solid; border-top-color: #d0d0d0; border-right-width: 1px; border-right-style: solid; border-right-color: #d0d0d0; border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-color: #d0d0d0; border-left-width: 1px; border-left-style: solid; border-left-color: #d0d0d0; background-color: #fafafa; } .card h2 { margin-top: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 8px; margin-left: 0px; } .card p { margin-top: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; }

classification.reason: Same anti-aliasing/hinting mismatch between Chromium's own text rasterizer and Florui's skrifa+tiny-skia one already calibrated for the bare-element fixtures; a real card compounds two text-bearing children instead of one but shares the same identical embedded font.
